name: Kyteler, Alice

sources: Davidson, L. S., and J. O. Ward. *The Sorcery Trial of Alice Kyteler*. Binghamton, N.Y.: Medieval and Renaissance Texts & Studies, 1993.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Alice Kyteler is an Irish heroine. She was a rich merchant of Kilkenny. Ireland saw no witch-burning hysteria like the rest of Europe. English and Scottish lands burned many, but Ireland stood apart. Only one woman was ever put to death for witchcraft there. That woman was Petronilla, the maid of Alice. In 1324 Bishop Richard Ledrede of Ossory accused Alice. She stood charged with her eleven friends and kin of witchcraft and heresy. Alice fled to England and lived out her days there. History never took note of her again. The case was the first to call witchcraft a heresy rooted in non-Christian belief.

okr.objective: Alice Kyteler escaped the first Irish witchcraft heresy trial.
